strategy_title: maxnreg Without Tile Change Causes Local Spill Regression
strategy_description: Applying maxnreg to cap register usage (168→128 registers/thread) without simultaneously reducing tile sizes forces the compiler to spill registers to local (stack) memory. This introduced uncoalesced local load/store traffic (only 1 of 32 bytes per sector utilized), increased total executed instructions by ~11% (4.13M→4.58M), and raised kernel duration from 36.58 µs to 43.94 µs despite theoretical occupancy improving from 18.75% to 25%. Achieved occupancy remained unchanged at ~6.25% because the grid (72 blocks) was still too small to fill 132 SMs, so the occupancy gain was irrelevant. The net effect was a 20% slowdown driven by register spill overhead.
applicable_when: Never apply maxnreg alone when the tile sizes (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) remain unchanged and the register budget reduction is large (>20%). This pattern reliably causes register spill.
do_not_apply_when: Do not apply maxnreg without simultaneously reducing tile sizes when: (1) the register reduction is >20% of original count, (2) the grid is already too small to benefit from higher occupancy (waves_per_sm < 0.5), or (3) the kernel has large per-thread working sets (large BLOCK_M * BLOCK_N accumulator tiles). In these cases, spill overhead will dominate any occupancy gain.
framework_notes: In Triton, maxnreg is passed as a per-Config argument to @triton.autotune. When maxnreg forces spill, NCU reports MemoryCacheAccessPattern OPT rules for local loads/stores with ~1 byte/32-byte sector utilization. The autotune overhead itself is not the cause — the spill is. CUDA equivalent: __launch_bounds__(block_size, min_blocks_per_sm) has the same spill risk when register budget is cut without reducing work per thread.

applicable_when: The dominant bottleneck is 7.9-way shared memory bank conflicts (69.43% of shared load wavefronts are conflicts), causing 39.3% of all stall cycles as MIO stalls. The root cause is the B matrix stride: stride_bn=192 (a multiple of 32 — the number of shared memory banks), so every warp column access maps to the same bank. The current BLOCK_K=32 means 32 K-elements are staged per iteration; with stride_bn=192, consecutive threads in the N-dimension all land on the same bank modulo 32. Increasing BLOCK_K to 64 halves the number of K-loop iterations (6→3 for K=192), reducing total shared memory staging operations by 50% and cutting MIO stall cycles proportionally. Simultaneously, reducing BLOCK_N from 128 to 64 doubles the grid from 72 to 144 blocks, covering more of the 132 SMs (1.09 waves vs 0.14 waves), directly addressing the LaunchConfiguration bottleneck. This tile reshape avoids the correctness failure seen in prior attempts (which changed BLOCK_M) and avoids the register spill seen with maxnreg-only changes.
